newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. says NATO to fix date for enlargement summit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says NATO to fix date for enlargement summit.

text.p: NATO foreign ministers meeting in Brussels on Tuesday and Wednesday will fix a date for a summit next year at which certain former communist states will be invited to open accession talks, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said on Monday.

"The meeting tomorrow will be significant in setting a date for that NATO summit next year and a full agenda of decisions for that summit," he told reporters. Diplomatic sources said the summit would be held in July in a European capital and the most likely current dates were July 7-9.

About 11 former satellites of the defunct Soviet Union in central and eastern Europe are clamouring to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) -- for years the West's defence bulwark against the Moscow-led Warsaw Pact.
Russia is resolutely opposed to plans to expand the alliance eastwards, warning it risks creating a new dividing line in Europe.

NATO foreign ministers, while insisting the enlargement timetable is non-negotiable, are also expected to adopt a declaration stressing the alliance has no intention of moving nuclear weapons on to the territory of any new members.
Poland, Hungary, and the Czech Republic are the three countries most likely to be asked to open membership talks, but Slovenia and Romania are also in the frame, diplomats say.
